questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared for the high cost of living in Seattle.

Enjoy the Seattle weather while you can — it changes quickly.

If you want to work with a professor on academic practice, reach out early and act fast.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Seek all the information you need well in advance, and be prepared for unexpected interruptions or changes along the way.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part was collaborating with researchers at NVIDIA Seattle on cutting-edge work in agentic long-horizon planning. I had the opportunity to engage in co-research, learn from industry experts, and contribute to real-world AI problems. This experience not only deepened my technical skills but also gave me valuable insight into how academic research connects with industrial applications in the field of large language models and autonomous agents.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was dealing with information mismatches and class schedule conflicts. Some course information I received in advance did not match the actual offerings, and several classes I planned to take overlapped in time. This required me to frequently adjust my study plan and make quick decisions with limited alternatives. Navigating these administrative and logistical hurdles while staying on track academically was definitely the toughest part of my exchange.
